notes: §1985:VIII.4.6.4 GR6: 'After the execution of the REWRITE statement is complete, the information in the area referenced by identifier-1 is available, even though the information in the area referenced by record-name-1 is not available except as specified by the SAME RECORD AREA clause'. The FROM phrase is an implicit MOVE whose sender identifier-1 is never written (MoveBinder.BindFromPhrase; KeyedIoEmitter.EmitRewrite and SequentialIoEmitter.EmitRewrite only send the record area), and a SAME RECORD AREA clause makes the files' records one storage area (FileControlBinder.LinkSameRecordArea, FileModel.SameRecordAreaPeers), so the released record stays visible through every peer. Witness: REWRITE FROM a WS record, WS still UPDATED. Probes: dynamic file in SAME RECORD AREA with a second relative file: after REWRITE FROM WS-REC, WS, RA and the peer RX all UPDATED; FROM TE(I) still SECOND2; FROM an OCCURS DEPENDING group (WC=3) still XYZ; a failed random REWRITE (23) leaves identifier-1 FAILED7; reread records UPDATED and XYZ. (c): REWRITE RA FROM RB (another record of the same FD, the case 2023 admits and §1985:VIII.4.6.3 SR1 forbids) compiles at 85: open as kb/Work PB5077 on that row.

next.reason: 1985 GR6 unconditionally: 'the information in the area referenced by identifier-1 is available'. §2023:14.9.35.4 GR10 adds 'provided that identifier-1 is not one or part of one of the record descriptions subordinate to the file-description'. 1985 SR1 refused identifier-1 sharing storage with record-name-1 (every record of the FD shares the record area); 2023 lifts that (§2023:14.9.35.4 GR7 NOTE 2 treats sharing as overlap), so a program 1985 refused is accepted and gets no availability guarantee: a case removed.
